title: Immunohistochemical Analysis of Ganglion Neurons Innervating the Lower Urinary Tract
author: Janet R Keast
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.w3efgje

steps.title: Cryoprotect tissues
steps.instruction: Cryoprotect tissues in phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS; 0.1 M, pH 7.2) containing 30 % sucrose at 4 °C for 24–72 hours prior to cutting.

steps.title: Embed and section tissues
steps.instruction: Embed tissues in a cryomold using OCT, freeze in a cryostat, cut 14 µm sections, and distribute sections progressively across sets of three slides so each slide receives non‑consecutive sections; use chrome‑alum treated slides pre‑coated (subbed) with 1 % gelatin, dry them, and store at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Embed tissue in OCT within a cryomold.
Freeze the embedded block in the cryostat.
Collect sections onto slides, arranging them in sets of three non‑consecutive sections per slide.
Pre‑coat chrome‑alum treated slides with 1 % gelatin.
Dry the coated slides and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Air‑dry slides
steps.instruction: Air‑dry slides at room temperature for at least 10 minutes.

steps.title: First PBS wash
steps.instruction: Wash sections in PBS for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Incubate sections in blocking solution at room temperature in a humidified dark chamber for 1–2 hours.

steps.title: Apply primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Dilute primary antibodies (or combinations) in hypertonic PBS and incubate sections for 18–24 hours in a humidified dark chamber.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash sections in PBS for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Apply secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Dilute secondary antibodies (or combinations) in hypertonic PBS and incubate sections for 2–3 hours in a humidified dark chamber.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash sections in PBS for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Count labeled neurons
steps.instruction: Count retrogradely labeled neurons and classify them according to immunoreactivity, including only nucleated neuronal profiles in the analysis.
